Population increased in Canterbury

The estimated population of Canterbury in 2024 was 162,100 usual residents, a rise of 0.8% since 2023.

This meant that Canterbury's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Canterbury increased by 3.5%.

Over this slightly longer period, Canterbury was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Canterbury

The average (median) age rose to 41.7 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Canterbury has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Canterbury is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Canterbury's population of 162,100 usual residents was made up of:

  • 26,148 people aged 0 to 15 years, (16.1%)
  • 99,758 people aged 16 to 64 years, (61.5%)
  • 36,194 people aged 65 years and over, (22.3%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Canterbury has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (22.3% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Canterbury, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Canterbury
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Canterbury, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 491 people (-0.3%). In total, there were 1,183 births and 1,674 deaths in Canterbury.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 1,096 (-0.7%). There were 14,658 people entering the area and 15,754 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Canterbury's population of 2,880 (1.8%) as a result of 4,708 people entering the area and 1,828 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Canterbury was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Canterbury in mid-2023 is 160,826.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 999 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 112 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 887 people.
